sections.label: The opening
sections.line: A second edition of the 2018 book
sections.para: Dinis's 2018 book Generation Z Developers is on Leanpub at 60%, read by 465 people, and on Amazon. Much of what he writes now is in it, mostly as outlines: 90 of 138 files. Those outlines have since been written as articles here, so he plans a second edition, keeping the name, for people getting into development and their first job.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: The book, its outlines, and a new edition
sections.para: Written in 2018 and left 60% complete, the book holds many current ideas as outlines that newsroom articles now answer. A second edition would keep the Generation Z name, since its readers are still that generation and are all developers now, and would be published with handwritten notes and a launch in Portugal.

sections.label: The book
sections.line: Generation Z Developers, as it stands
sections.para: Subtitled key concepts and ideas for the next generation of developers, it is on Leanpub at 60% complete, 136 pages and 30,695 words, last updated on 8 October 2018 with 465 readers, also on Amazon, with its source on GitHub. It was written in Markdown, in Git, in public, with GitHub issues for feedback; decent, unfinished and full of spelling mistakes.

sections.label: What it said
sections.line: One competitive advantage, and act like part of the company
sections.para: The book worried that Generation Z, born after 1996, had missed how technology came to work. Its job chapter said the best way to get a job is one competitive advantage, once using a computer or the internet, and to act like part of the company by collaborating on its open source. It also said to learn AI within five years; ChatGPT came four years later.

sections.label: What held, and what did not
sections.line: What held and what did not
sections.para: Held: one competitive advantage, now agentic workflows; act like part of the company; publish; GitHub as your CV; your future self; pioneers, settlers and town planners. Did not: the dated list of tools to learn; the advice to learn how to program AI, when using and directing it mattered more; and a narrow idea of who counts as a developer.

sections.label: The outlines have been written
sections.para: Of the 138 files, 90 are outlines, including all eight on security and 26 of 27 on concepts. Many read like briefs the newsroom later wrote without planning it: future self as bringing my past work back, publish as your own newsroom, graphs as the graphs books, GitHub as your CV as act as the job you want. Written chapters have newer answers too.

sections.label: The name
sections.line: Keep Generation Z in the title
sections.para: Should it become Generation AI Developers? Dinis's view, argued here, is to keep the name: the people he wants to give it to are still Generation Z, the oldest now 30, and the play on the name works better than before, because with agents they are all developers. A subtitle can carry what changed.

sections.label: The second edition
sections.para: Keep and finish what held, fixing the spelling; add a then and now for chapters that changed; fill each outline from the newsroom articles that answer it, rewritten for this reader; add a part on working with agents; and include Dinis's scanned handwritten notes, as with the other books.

sections.label: How, and when
sections.line: Books from articles, KDP and Portugal
sections.para: The method follows books from articles: map chapters to articles, write the gaps here first, assemble, and publish on Amazon KDP, where Dinis has published before, so the shorter review applies. It may be the book to launch in Portugal during Web Summit, as the manual he would hand to people for development and for getting a job. A build note and briefs entry exist.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.line: A plan, not a book yet
sections.para: Nothing of the second edition is written. The outline-to-article map is a first reading, and not every outline has an article. Which book comes first for Web Summit is still open. The Amazon listing itself was not read for the article.

sections.label: Where this comes from
sections.line: Leanpub, the repository and a memo
sections.para: From Dinis's voice memo of 18 October 2026, the book's Leanpub page read that day for completeness, length, readers and date, and its repository, cloned and read with every file counted and quotations taken from its chapters.
